content.scenario: The Central Authority receives a complaint against a company for violating consumer rights. The Director-General, appointed under sub-section (2) of section 15, conducts an inquiry or investigation under this Act as directed by the Central Authority.
content.outcome: The Director-General, with the power to delegate powers to other officers, conducts the inquiry or investigation, and submits a report to the Central Authority. The Director-General may also call upon a person, direct them to produce documents or records, and enter and search premises to gather evidence.

user_queries: What are the powers of the Director-General under the Consumer Protection Act?
Can the Director-General delegate powers to other officers?
What is the role of the Director-General in the Central Authority?
